item.title: Patrick Mahomes Could Get New WR Ahead of NFL Trade Deadline
item.description: The Kansas City Chiefs are rumored to be on the lookout for a wide receiver ahead of the NFL trade deadline. They continue to be linked to the Jacksonville Jaguars’ Brian Thomas Jr., who could be Patrick Mahomes’ new wideout. Thomas is in his third NFL season. He entered the league as the No. 23 overall pick in 2024 out of LSU. The Louisiana native finished his rookie campaign with 87 receptions for 1,282 yards and 10 touchdowns, earning Pro Bowl honors. He saw action in 14 games last year and experienced a slight dip in his numbers. Thomas recorded 48 receptions for 707 yards and two touchdowns, including one in the Wild Card Round loss to the Buffalo Bills. Meanwhile, Kansas City has lost back-to-back games after starting the season 5-0. They are coming off a 28-24 defeat to the Denver Broncos in Week 9 despite Mahomes’ strong performance. He completed 30-of-41 passes for 321 yards, three touchdowns and zero interceptions. Kansas City Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes (15) looks to pass the ball against the Seattle Seahawks during the first quarter at Lumen Field. Patrick Mahomes And the Chiefs Could Trade For Brian Thomas Jr. ESPN’s Adam Schefter and Ian Rapoport reported on Saturday that the Chiefs are “intrigued” by Thomas. Several analysts consider the wide receiver position as the team’s “weak spot” despite having a high-octane offense led by Patrick Mahomes. “Thomas played only 19 snaps during Thursday night’s victory in Baltimore and did not catch a pass. The Kansas City Chiefs have continued to be intrigued by Thomas,” Schefter and Rapoport wrote. The team has Xavier Worthy as its WR1. However, they don’t have depth behind him and also signed Jacob De Jesus to the practice squad recently. He’ll likely serve as an insurance if the Chiefs fail to add another wideout. Thomas fits their need as he is young and has shown glimpses of his true potential. But the front office still a lot of maneuvering and calls to make before potentially landing him. item.description: 'A lot of coaches are afraid': Ryan ten Doeschate opens up on 'calling out' Virat Kohli during India star's struggles in Australia originally appeared on Cricket News . KEY TAKEAWAYS: Former India assistant coach Ryan ten Doeschate says he intervened with Virat Kohli during the fourth Test of the 2024-25 series in Australia . He waited for a rain break to raise it and spent time working out how to deliver it. Kohli was caught behind or in the slips in eight of his nine dismissals on that tour. Ryan ten Doeschate reveals the courage it took to confront Virat Kohli For someone of his calibre, Virat Kohli's last few years in Test cricket were very different from his peak. His struggles on the fifth-stump line, his regression against spin and his inability to hit boundaries continued to trouble him throughout the New Zealand and Australia tours. His problem in Australia in 2024-25 was especially visible to everyone watching, which is precisely what made it difficult for those paid to fix it. Ryan ten Doeschate, India's assistant coach on that tour, has described how long he sat on it before saying anything. "I actually was just telling a really great story about Virat and his troubles he had in Australia with driving the ball and nicking off," Ten Doeschate said in a recent interview on talkSPORT . "Eventually in the fourth Test I went to intervene and chat to him, and he was brilliant about it, and he actually wanted someone to chat to him." "I think a lot of coaches are afraid to make interventions because it can be seen that you are being, you know, trying to justify your job, or you're interfering or just saying things for the sake of saying it," he said. He acknowledged the risk runs both ways, since a badly judged intervention can leave a batter worse off than silence would. "You've got to strike the balance of making an intervention that's going to help the player or confusing them." "I never want to be a coach who's scared of an opinion of someone else for stepping in, for saying the right thing," he said, before adding that the modern game pushes the other way. Melbourne, where the intervention happened, contained both versions of the problem. Kohli made 36 from 88 balls in the first innings, leaving well for long stretches, and added 102 with Yashasvi Jaiswal before nicking Scott Boland to Alex Carey shortly after Jaiswal was run out. In the second innings, he lasted 29 balls for five, flashing at Mitchell Starc to Usman Khawaja at first slip with India 33 for 3, and they lost by 184 runs. item.title: Why Josh Acheampong Missed Chelsea vs Sunderland
item.description: IMAGO / Pro Sports Images Crystal Palace v Chelsea Premier League 04/01/2025. Chelsea defender Josh-Kofi Acheampong 34 during the Premier League match between Crystal Palace and Chelsea at Selhurst Park, London, England on 4 January 2025.… | Source: Lastwordonsports.com - Alex Richards, LWOF Editor When the lineups were released for Chelsea vs Sunderland it was immediately noticeable that the Blues had made some unexpected moves. The no-striker formation was used again with a midfield three of Moises Caicedo, Romeo Lavia, and Jordan Henderson backing up three attackers/wingers. In addition, the back line looked brand new and a little bare with Josh Acheampong not involved in the squad at all. The Cobham graduate has been a regular in this campaign so his total absence was clear to any fan. Read More: Chelsea vs Sunderland Confirmed Lineups Josh Acheampong Status Confirmed Following Chelsea vs Sunderland Absence IMAGO / Every Second Media Latest Report Nizaar Kinsella has provided the latest update on the young defender. It is described as a small issue that likely won’t impact future matches. This comes as good news as the homegrown defender has been used as a versatile right-sided defender who can shift between a back three and back four as needed. His absence along with the injury to Reece James leaves the side without a proven versatile player for that side of the back line. All in all, it could have been far worse. The manager will be happy to have Acheampong back for the match with Leeds in a few weeks time. The Last Word With the back line already hurting, this is another problem for Xabi Alonso to handle that will give him headaches. He was already without captain James and experienced, expensive centre back Maxence Lacroix. Losing Acheampong adds to the headache as he was a versatile piece who can alternate from right centre-back to right back depending on game state and tactical setup. With the injury to Joao Pedro and the absence of Emi Martinez already impacting the team in goal and up front, the crisis in the back line is a tenuous balancing act that could cause a poor run of form if more dominoes continue to fall. Luckily, this one seems to be a short term issue that won’t see the English youth miss many matches. Other Football Content Every Chelsea Wonderkid in Football Manager 27 Ranked Who is Paris Brunner? item.description: The Baltimore Ravens are facing a difficult stretch after losing their starting quarterback to another injury. Their problems continued in NFL Week 9, when they suffered a 33-10 defeat to the Jacksonville Jaguars for their fourth consecutive loss. Lamar Jackson ‘s absence has left Baltimore searching for answers at quarterback. The team now faces a lengthy wait before it can realistically expect its two-time MVP to return. The injury occurred during Baltimore’s 36-10 loss to the Buffalo Bills on Nov. 1. Jackson suffered the damage on his first offensive snap when his throwing hand collided with a defender during a pass attempt . Lamar Jackson is out 6-9 weeks with a fractured and dislocated thumb. But the former MVP has vowed to return — assuming Baltimore stays alive. The Ravens subsequently placed him on injured reserve, guaranteeing he would miss at least four games. Jackson had only just returned from a left ankle injury that kept him out of three games. His latest setback means the Ravens must once again adjust their plans around his absence. Lamar Jackson tells Ravens teammates he plans to return Despite the lengthy recovery timeline, Jackson has not given up on playing again this season. Jackson has told his teammates that he intends to return later this season. His message to the locker room was simple “Just stay alive” (h/t NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport) . The team acquired Jacoby Brissett from the Arizona Cardinals to strengthen its quarterback options during Jackson’s absence. item.title: Browns Week 9: Result against Saints could be huge
item.description: The Cleveland Browns’ matchup against the New Orleans Saints is a significant game in the context of their season. The team is currently 5-3 and will either continue climbing toward the top of the AFC or continue to fall back into the pack . The team needs to show it can bounce back after a tough loss. item.title: Stephen Curry and Golden State Warriors break 76-year-old NBA record with 7-3 start to the season
item.description: Photo by Ezra Shaw/Getty Images After a shaky start to the season, the Golden State Warriors have surprised many fans with their form across their first 10 games. The Warriors went 0-3 in their first three games, with many fans believing that analysts were correct about their weaknesses costing them this season. However, since then, the Warriors have turned things around in a major way, winning seven games in a row following their latest victory over the Orlando Magic. Golden State Warriors break Boston Celtics’ 1950-51 record As mentioned earlier, with their win over the Orlando Magic, the Golden State Warriors have won their last seven games and have put up a 7-3 record in their opening 10 games. After starting the season 0-3, few would have expected them to turn their fortunes around this quickly and in such dominant fashion. And in doing so, the Warriors have become the first team since the 1950-51 Boston Celtics to go 7-3 in their first 10 games after going 0-3 to start the season. That Celtics team was coached by legendary head coach Red Auerbach, with star point guard Bob Cousy running the offence. The Celtics would get knocked out in the first round of the playoffs that season, losing in a best-of-three series to the New York Knicks. The Warriors will be hoping their start to the season across the first 10 games is where the similarities between the two sides lie, as they will be hoping to make a deep run in the playoffs. Stephen Curry’s brilliant scoring performances have played a huge role in their recent turnaround, as has the incredible form of rookie Yaxel Lendeborg. Thanks to their strong start, the Warriors are the fourth seed in the Western Conference, behind the Oklahoma City Thunder, San Antonio Spurs, and LA Lakers, all of whom have started the season 8-2. In fact, those three teams and the Philadelphia 76ers in the Eastern Conference are the only teams in the NBA with a better record than the Warriors. item.title: Jason Witten opens up about whirlwind week as new Sooner offensive coordinator
item.description: Mandatory Credit: Matt Pendleton-Imagn Images Jason Witten opens up about whirlwind week as new Sooner offensive coordinator appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Following Oklahoma’s offensive struggles, head coach Brent Venables made a significant coaching change by appointing Jason Witten as interim offensive coordinator. Despite his limited experience at the collegiate level, the former NFL tight end quickly embraced the unexpected responsibility and focused on uniting the Sooners during a challenging stretch of the season. Speaking with Colton Sulley of The Oklahoman, Witten addressed the team’s struggles and explained the message he delivered to his players during the transition. “Ultimately, we haven’t coached very well and haven’t gotten the results we wanted,” Witten said. “I told them what they could expect from me.” Asked #Sooners interim offensive coordinator Jason Witten about his whirlwind week. pic.twitter.com/LLlPO6UFSp Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) — Colton Sulley (@colton_sulley) November 8, 2026 Witten also made it clear that he wanted players committed to the challenge. He understood that some might question the coaching change. However, he urged them to focus on moving forward as a team. This came after Oklahoma’s response following its loss to South Carolina . “Hey, listen, you don’t want to be here. I understand that. Go see coach Venables. But here’s what we’re (going to) do — we’re (going to) figure it out,” Witten told the players. The interim coordinator also stressed the importance of responding to adversity with the right mindset. He challenged the Sooners to approach the situation with purpose and take responsibility. Witten reminded them that fixing their struggles would require a united effort. “This wasn’t one person doing this. This is about the team,” Witten explained. His message seemed to connect with the locker room. Oklahoma’s players quickly rallied behind their new coordinator. After the game, they even doused Witten with Gatorade during the celebration. The moment highlighted the support he had earned in a short time. It also capped a demanding week for the former NFL tight end. item.title: 'Abolish ICE': Austin FC captain, citing rift with fans, makes bold proclamation
item.description: KANSAS CITY, KANSAS - OCTOBER 24: Ilie Sanchez #6 of Austin FC controls the ball during the first half against Sporting Kansas City at Sporting Park on October 24, 2026 in Kansas City, Kansas. (Photo by Jay Biggerstaff/Getty Images) (Jay Biggerstaff/Getty Images) If Saturday was Ilie Sanchez's last time speaking to the media as an Austin FC player , he certainly didn't hold anything back. Sanchez, who was Austin FC's captain the last two seasons and is likely to become a free agent this winter, said he is in favor of abolishing ICE following the Verde and Black's 2-0 loss to Portland at Q2 Stadium in their MLS season finale. "I would personally like to say: abolish ICE," Sanchez said. "That's what the biggest issue has been lately. And looking at the future, I think that when we had the union between the supporters and Austin FC, we were unstoppable. Or at least you could see a different vibe or even different performances. That's my humble opinion. I hope that things improve and things get better, and things get where this club deserves and the supporters deserve. I would like to leave saying 'thank you' because it's been a pleasure to be a part of this team and city." MORE: Austin FC responds to walkout after removal of fan with "Abolish Ice" shirt Austin FC and anti-ICE demonstrations Austin FC received considerable backlash online and from its fans following the Sept. 26 removal of former city council candidate Daniela Silva from Q2 Stadium for violating the venue policy that states, "Signs, symbols, or images displayed for commercial purposes for electioneering, campaigning or advocating for or against any candidate, political party, legislative issues or government action is prohibited." Silva was wearing an "Abolish ICE" shirt inside the stadium about a week after a federal immigration officer shot a Venezuelan food delivery driver in Austin. Some supporters' groups staged a walkout shortly after kickoff the next home match Oct. 10 against Nashville and have urged the club in social media postings to take action - and even publicly come out against the federal agency - on issues involving U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement. Austin FC released a statement expressing support for its fans and the immigrant community but did not go as far as Sanchez did Saturday. Sanchez, 35, is from Barcelona, Spain and has played in MLS since 2017. Austin FC has an option to renew his contract for 2027, but given his age, declining play and speaking of his time with the club in the past tense, that seems unlikely. item.title: Red Sox's Former Interest in Cubs Ace Could Lead to Offseason Signing Now
item.description: Red Sox's Former Interest in Cubs Ace Could Lead to Offseason Signing Now originally appeared on NESN . Add NESN as a Preferred Source by clicking here . A lot of the focus for the Boston Red Sox in the early stages of the offseason, at least from the fan base, has been centered around how they're going to improve on the offensive side of the baseball. I don't disagree with that at all, as the Red Sox have a need to improve in that area. However, it's also fair to mention that Boston is going to be a team that tries to improve on the mound as well. With the Red Sox being a contending team, squads can never have enough starting pitching, specifically, and with the possibility of losing Sonny Gray, it feels very likely that Craig Breslow is going to do what's necessary to add a starter. According to the latest report, there was a player that the Red Sox were interested in a couple of years ago when he came over to America. That guy is none other than Shota Imanaga, the Chicago Cubs' left-handed free agent. "Even if the rotation looks to be a strong suit, you can never count out [Craig Breslow] from adding more rotation depth, particularly if Gray signs elsewhere," Ian Browne wrote . "One name that intrigues me? Shota Imanaga. Breslow was really fond of him when he was scouting him for the Cubs three years ago. The Cubs wound up signing him, but Breslow was in his early stages with the Red Sox at that point." Imanaga is a very difficult player to evaluate at times because of his questionable number of home runs allowed each year. He's coming off a year in which he allowed 35 bombs, and it wasn't like he was much better in the previous two seasons, allowing 27 and 31. When he came over from Japan, there were many questions about whether he was going to keep the ball in the yard. Unfortunately, that question is still there, and at 33 years old, it doesn't look like that's going to change. item.title: Dodgers notes: Tarik Skubal, Josue De Paula
item.description: LOS ANGELES, CA - OCTOBER 03: Los Angeles Dodgers starting pitcher Tarik Skubal (29) pitches in the first inning during the National League Divisional Series game between the Los Angeles Dodgers and the Atlanta Braves on October 03, 2026 at Dodger Stadium in Los Angeles. (Photo by David Dennis/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images It has been 10 days since the 2026 season concluded with the Milwaukee Brewers winning their first World Series championship in franchise history. Unsurprisingly, there haven’t been any major moves that have drastically changed the landscape of the sport, and until that first spark is ignited, we must sit back and wait patiently as the offseason trudges on. The main concern for the Dodgers this offseason is the status of free agent Tarik Skubal, and they aren’t the only ones vying for his services. Teams like the New York Mets, Chicago Cubs and San Diego Padres have all expressed interest in signing the still-reigning two-time American League Cy Young award winner, but the details surrounding a potential contract are mirky. The Dodgers have already shown over the last three years that they are willing to hand out long-term contracts with record-breaking annual salaries while also dishing out short-term deals with inflated annual values. Katie Woo of The Athletic spoke with A.J. Pierzynski of the Foul Territory podcast about what type of deal Skubal will sign, where she envisions the Dodgers giving Skubal a contract more similar to that of Kyle Tucker rather than Yoshinobu Yamamoto. “I don’t see the Dodgers shelling out the long-term mega contract for the same reasons they didn’t to for Kyle Tucker. Andrew Friedman wants to prolong the team’s competitive window… Could we see a similar structure to what the Dodgers offered Kyle Tucker— shorter term with a much higher AAV— as their option? That’s certainly the thought process going into the GM Meetings.” Skubal will be entering his age-30 season in 2027, and Thomas Harrigan of MLB.com writes about how pitchers with historic dominance in their 20’s have fared once they are on the wrong side of 30. Whether Skubal’s next contract looks like a success will depend on his ability to stay on the mound. But chances are he still has at least a few Cy Young-caliber seasons ahead. In an effort to break out of camp next year, Josue De Paula is doing everything in his power to ensure that he can be a viable defensive option in the outfield, and that includes working with former Gold Glove award winner and 2018 World Series champion Jackie Bradley Jr., reports Dylan Hernandez of the California Post .

item.title: NFL Experts Pick Against Patriots in Green Bay Showdown, but Not Everyone Is Convinced
item.description: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Expert analysts across three major networks are picking the underdog Packers to knock of the Patriots in Gillette Stadium by a 17-6 margin. The New England Patriots are slight favorites heading into Sunday’s showdown with the Green Bay Packers at Gillette Stadium, but apparently not everyone is buying into New England’s resurgence. Despite identical 5-3 records and both teams winning four of their last five games, a significant majority of experts at ESPN and NFL.com are picking Green Bay to leave Foxborough with a victory. Across three major national prediction panels — ESPN, CBS Sports and NFL.com — 17 of 23 analysts are backing the Packers. Read Next 5 Keys to a New England Patriots Victory Over the Green Bay Packers in Week 9 The disconnect between the betting market and the national media is one of the more interesting storylines surrounding Sunday’s 4:25 p.m. ET kickoff. The Patriots are three-point favorites, according to the odds listed by NFL.com, yet some of the most recognizable NFL analysts believe Jordan Love and the Packers will prevail over Drake Maye and New England. Here’s a closer look at who’s picking whom, and why. ESPN Experts Overwhelmingly Favor Green Bay ESPN’s 11-member prediction panel has delivered one of the strongest votes of confidence for the Packers. Nine analysts picked Green Bay, with only Mike Clay and Dan Graziano choosing New England. Among those backing the Packers are Matt Bowen, Jeremy Fowler, Ben Solak, Eric Moody, Jason Reid, Kalyn Kahler, Pamela Maldonado, Lindsey Thiry and Seth Wickersham. However, ESPN Patriots reporter Mike Reiss sees things differently. Reiss predicts a 27-24 Patriots victory, pointing to the importance of New England’s secondary against Green Bay’s passing attack. “CB Christian Gonzalez will need to bring his ‘A’ game,” Reiss wrote in his prediction, as published in the Patriots’ expert picks roundup . That matchup could be decisive against Love, who has been one of the league’s most dangerous deep-ball passers this season. NFL.com Analysts Pick Packers 4-1, but One Expert Sees a Major Weakness Four of NFL.com’s five analysts predict a Green Bay victory, although all five expect a competitive game. Jeremy Bergman picks the Packers 20-17, Gennaro Filice predicts a 27-23 Green Bay victory, Bobby Kownack has the Packers winning 24-23, and Dan Parr forecasts a 26-24 result. The New England Patriots are slight favorites heading into Sunday’s showdown with the Green Bay Packers at Gillette Stadium, but apparently not everyone is buying into New England’s resurgence. Despite identical 5-3 records and both teams winning four of their last five games, a significant majority of experts at ESPN and NFL.com are picking Green Bay to leave Foxborough with a victory. Across three major national prediction panels — ESPN, CBS Sports and NFL.com — 17 of 23 analysts are backing the Packers. Read Next 5 Keys to a New England Patriots Victory Over the Green Bay Packers in Week 9 The disconnect between the betting market and the national media is one of the more interesting storylines surrounding Sunday’s 4:25 p.m. ET kickoff. The Patriots are three-point favorites, according to the odds listed by NFL.com, yet some of the most recognizable NFL analysts believe Jordan Love and the Packers will prevail over Drake Maye and New England. Here’s a closer look at who’s picking whom, and why. ESPN Experts Overwhelmingly Favor Green Bay ESPN’s 11-member prediction panel has delivered one of the strongest votes of confidence for the Packers. Nine analysts picked Green Bay, with only Mike Clay and Dan Graziano choosing New England. Among those backing the Packers are Matt Bowen, Jeremy Fowler, Ben Solak, Eric Moody, Jason Reid, Kalyn Kahler, Pamela Maldonado, Lindsey Thiry and Seth Wickersham. However, ESPN Patriots reporter Mike Reiss sees things differently. Reiss predicts a 27-24 Patriots victory, pointing to the importance of New England’s secondary against Green Bay’s passing attack. “CB Christian Gonzalez will need to bring his ‘A’ game,” Reiss wrote in his prediction, as published in the Patriots’ expert picks roundup . That matchup could be decisive against Love, who has been one of the league’s most dangerous deep-ball passers this season. NFL.com Analysts Pick Packers 4-1, but One Expert Sees a Major Weakness Four of NFL.com’s five analysts predict a Green Bay victory, although all five expect a competitive game. Jeremy Bergman picks the Packers 20-17, Gennaro Filice predicts a 27-23 Green Bay victory, Bobby Kownack has the Packers winning 24-23, and Dan Parr forecasts a 26-24 result. Brooke Cersosimo is the lone NFL.com analyst backing New England, predicting a 24-20 Patriots victory. Her reasoning centers on Green Bay’s inability to establish a consistent running game. The Packers enter Sunday averaging an NFL-worst 60.6 rushing yards per game, while New England has allowed just 92.6 rushing yards per contest. Cersosimo believes that imbalance will eventually catch up with Green Bay. “It’s a weakness the Packers have been able to overcome in past weeks, but it’ll catch up to them this time,” she wrote in NFL.com’s Week 9 predictions . Her analysis provides one of the strongest arguments for a New England victory: If the Patriots can make Green Bay one-dimensional, they could force Love into difficult passing situations. CBS Sports Experts Are More Divided The seven-member CBS Sports panel is nearly evenly split, with four analysts backing Green Bay and three predicting a Patriots victory. Pete Prisco, Jared Dubin, John Breech and Tyler Sullivan picked the Packers. Ryan Wilson, Dave Richard and Jamey Eisenberg chose New England. Prisco anticipates a defensive struggle and predicts Green Bay will escape with a 19-16 victory. “This has the feel of a low-scoring game with two good defenses,” Prisco wrote. He believes Green Bay’s additional rest after playing the previous Thursday will prove beneficial, with Love making the difference in the closing minutes. Prisco’s prediction is particularly interesting because it contrasts with the expectations of those who believe Maye and Love could produce an offensive showcase. Pro Football Talk’s Mike Florio Makes a Bold Patriots Prediction While much of the national media is leaning toward Green Bay, Pro Football Talk’s Mike Florio is decidedly more optimistic about New England. Florio predicts a 31-21 Patriots victory, one of the more decisive New England wins forecast by a prominent national analyst. That prediction stands in sharp contrast to the narrow margins projected by most of the NFL.com and CBS Sports panels. If Florio is correct, the Patriots would not only defeat another playoff contender but do so by double digits. Patriots Insiders Expect a Close Victory The Patriots’ own media analysts are unanimous in picking New England, although each expects a tight contest. Paul Perillo predicts a 24-23 Patriots victory, believing Green Bay’s struggles in the kicking game could become a factor. Mike Dussault forecasts a 28-27 New England win, with the battle between the defensive fronts and opposing offensive lines playing a central role. Evan Lazar expects the Patriots to win 23-20 on a late field goal by Andy Borregales. “I think we’re in for a classic at Gillette Stadium on Sunday that’s a true coin-flip game,” Lazar wrote. He also acknowledged the difficulty of separating two teams that have followed remarkably similar paths through the first eight games. The predictions reflect both confidence in the Patriots’ progress and an understanding that Green Bay represents a significant challenge. The Athletic and Sports Illustrated Panels Are Split Other national outlets are far less convinced that Green Bay is the obvious choice. At The Athletic, four of seven analysts picked the Packers, while three favored the Patriots. Sports Illustrated’s MMQB panel went the other direction, with five of eight experts selecting New England. Among the MMQB analysts picking the Patriots were Mike Kadlick, Gilberto Manzano, Matt Verderame, Eva Geitheim and John Pluym. That split reinforces the notion that Sunday’s matchup is far closer than ESPN’s lopsided prediction panel might suggest. What the Expert Predictions Really Tell Us The most revealing aspect of the national predictions isn’t simply that more analysts favor Green Bay. It’s that most expect the game to be decided by a handful of points. All five NFL.com predictions have margins of four points or fewer. Prisco sees a three-point Packers victory. Reiss predicts a three-point Patriots win. The experts generally agree on one thing: These are two closely matched teams with talented young quarterbacks and defenses capable of influencing the outcome. But they disagree about which team is better equipped to overcome its weaknesses. Green Bay has struggled to run the football, putting additional pressure on Love. New England must find ways to protect Maye and generate offense without several key playmakers. There is also the matter of home-field advantage, which could prove important in a game expected to remain competitive into the fourth quarter. The Patriots have an opportunity to prove the national skeptics wrong Sunday afternoon. And if New England defeats Green Bay, it will have done so against a team that many of the country’s most prominent NFL analysts expected to win. Need One Prediction to Hang Your Hat On? You can call us homers if you want, but we’ve done our homework and Patriots Football Now is calling it for New England, 24-21. item.title: Germany drops threat to hand back ice hockey worlds over Russia ruling
item.description: FILE PHOTO - Finland's Kaapo Kakko (R) and Russia's Mikhail Sergachyov clash during the 2019 IIHF Ice Hockey World Championship semifinal ice hockey match between Russia and Finland at the Ondrej Nepela Arena. (is associated with: «Germany drops threat to hand back ice hockey worlds over Russia ruling») Jussi Nukari/STT-Lehtikuva/dpa Giving back the hosting rights to the 2027 men's world championship because of Russia's possible inclusion is no longer an option for Germany, the country's ice hockey boss said on Sunday. "We want to hold the world championship in Germany next year, and I am also very optimistic that we will manage that," German Ice Hockey Federation (DEB) chief executive Frank Lutz told reporters. The Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) ruled last month that Russia could take part in international ice hockey competitions again despite its long war in Ukraine. The judgement could have implications for other sports after the International Olympic Committee last year opened the door for Russia to return to the sporting fold. The International Ice Hockey Federation (IIHF) had argued security concerns meant Russia should still be excluded, but Russia appealed and won at CAS. Lutz and the German government then considered handing back the hosting rights to May's event, but ticket sales will now carry on as planned. A withdrawal would come with financial penalties and could damage Munich's bid for the Olympics. The IIHF recently said it would take a diplomatic route following the CAS ruling, which Lutz welcomes. Media reports say Russia is being persuaded to pull out after some nations and sponsors threatened a boycott. "We have seven or eight nations that have declared they do not want to play against a Russian team at the world championship. That makes a 16-nation world championship impossible," Lutz said. "The CAS ruling obliges the IIHF to readmit Russia. That is something we reject for many reasons. German politics rejects that too." Germany refusing visas for Russian players is one option available. An under-20 men's championship is taking place in Canada at the end of the year and Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney has said Russians will not attend, without specifying the details. The Swiss ice hockey federation said on Sunday that its team would not face Russia in the Canadian junior tournament.

item.title: “Still Need Brain Development”: CFB Fans React to Darian Mensah Running the “Worst 2 Min Drill” As Miami Loses 31–24 to Notre Dame
item.description: “Still Need Brain Development”: CFB Fans React to Darian Mensah Running the “Worst 2 Min Drill” As Miami Loses 31–24 to Notre Dame Darian Mensah may apparently need some more seasoning before being considered a top quarterback prospect. During the closing stages of Saturday’s game against Notre Dame, the Miami quarterback botched the final drive, forgetting to spike the ball with 13 seconds left. It resulted in a 24-31 loss for the Hurricanes and much ridicule from fans: Mensah finished with 24 completions for 302 yards and three touchdowns, but also an interception. Two of those scores went to Cooper Barkate, who had 118 yards on 10 catches. Elija Lofton took the other as part of his 113-yard outing. Meanwhile, CJ Carr led the Fighting Irish with 29/40 for 319 yards and three touchdowns. Micah Gilbert had two of those scores. Darian Mensah speaks after Miami’s loss to Notre Dame After the game, Darian Mensah addressed the media. He said about the defeat ( via CaneSport Miami Football’s YouTube channel ): “This one definitely stings, and like I said earlier, we’ve got to use it. But like you said, everything we want is still in front of us. We’ve got to stay positive and be ready to come to work Monday.” He added: “We’ve got to start faster. I’ve got to play better. We can’t turn it over. I know the situation, and I’m really just hurting for our guys right now.” Miami hosts Duke next Saturday. Kickoff is at 12 p.m. ET. item.title: 3 takeaways from Alabama's crucial road win vs. LSU
item.description: Alabama picked up a crucial win on Saturday as they pulled away to defeat LSU, 31-13 , in Tiger Stadium. It was tight for most of the game, and one in which the box score does not necessarily match the final score, but it is a win for Alabama nonetheless. The Tide improved to 7-2 (5-2 SEC), and with results elsewhere, are now right back in a tie in the loss column for a spot in the SEC title game. Alabama also dealt a crushing blow to LSU's College Football Playoff (CFP) hopes by dealing the Tigers a third loss. It was basically a must-win game for Alabama, and the Tide did what they had to do to win it. Here are three takeaways from Alabama's huge road win. Alabama's bend-don't-break defense It is not often that a team is outgained 457-285 and have less than half as many first downs as your opponent, and yet you win by 18. That's what happened on Saturday for Alabama though. And a lot of it had to do with their defense bending, but not breaking and making plays when they had to keep LSU out of the end zone. LSU had two turnover on downs inside the Alabama 10-yard line, and settled for a field goal on another trip inside the Tide's 10. LSU made it to inside the Alabama 40-yard line on eight of their 10 drives, but mustered just the one touchdown and two field goals. A big reason for that is that LSU was 0-for-4 on fourth down. Alabama's defense made plays when plays needed to be made. Ryan Coleman-Williams makes plays in return Ryan Coleman-Williams returned from injury on Saturday and made a couple key plays. His biggest play came in the fourth quarter on a punt return. LSU was punting with Alabama ahead 17-13, and Coleman-Williams sprung loose for a 32-yard return which set up a one play touchdown drive on a 25-yard pass to Cedarian Morgan which pushed Alabama's lead to 24-13. He also scored earlier in the game on an end-around in which LSU lost him. In the passing game, he ended up with just two catches for 14 yards, but he made his impact felt. Alabama proves CFP committee right Most of the talk surrounding Alabama this week was about their ranking in the initial CFP committee rankings in which they were ranked No. 5, a spot most felt was too-high. With all of that noise, Alabama responded with a big win over a top 15 team in LSU. This win puts Alabama in a great spot when it comes to the playoffs, but also potentially quiets some of the noise surrounding their ranking and arguably proved the committee correct in their bullishness on the Tide. item.title: Julián Alvarez’s Atlético redemption arc in full focus for visit of Barcelona
item.description: Top spot is up for grabs in Sunday’s heavyweight clash as the Spider faces the team that tried to trap him last summer Julián Alvarez said sorry but forgiveness must be earned on the field and Sunday would be the perfect place. At 9pm at the Metropolitano, Atlético Madrid play Barcelona. It is the biggest match in Spain right now, a place at the top of the table awaiting the winner; it is also the game the striker they call the Spider planned to play on the other side. That, Alvarez said in Dallas, was his “dream”. Denied that, he must defeat the men he wanted to join to win back the supporters he wanted to walk out on, no better opportunity than now. He has beaten them before. Last season, Atlético knocked Barcelona out of the Copa del Rey and Champions League . Alvarez scored both times but beneath the surface something had shifted in him and by the time the World Cup came round he admitted his desire to leave for Catalonia. That day, after Argentina beat Algeria, he didn’t name Barcelona and he didn’t need to; everyone knew. “It’s not the time to talk about this but nor can I hide,” he said. “I spoke with the people I needed to and the best thing for everyone is a transfer.” Continue reading...

item.title: There are very few reasons for Unai Emery to leave Aston Villa for Manchester United | Jonathan Wilson
item.description: Spaniard may feel some of Old Trafford’s allure when he goes there on Sunday but he is right in wanting to stay at the club with brighter prospects On Sunday afternoon, shortly before 4.30, Unai Emery will leave the tunnel at Old Trafford and walk along the touchline towards the bench. Will he glance around the grand old stadium – faded and leaking though it may be in parts – and think that he could have a part in restoring the club to former glories? Will he look at the home bench and imagine himself sitting there – or perhaps more plausibly, scuttling up and down in front of it – as the first Manchester United manager since Sir Alex Ferguson to land a league title? Perhaps not. Emery is, after all, in “advanced talks” to extend a contract at Villa that already runs to 2029. However frustrating he may find the habitual summer churn, he is good at managing it. He feels the right fit for Villa, and that is arguably the most important factor in determining success. Yet all elite managers share a robust self-belief and there is a paradoxical sense that the worse the situation gets at United, the more appealing the job becomes. Continue reading...

item.title: Martin Ødegaard extends Arsenal lead at top with winner to break Hull resistance
item.description: As most Arsenal supporters would testify, patience is a virtue. They needed plenty during the 22-year wait to be crowned Premier League champions and Mikel Arteta’s side certainly had to retain their composure as they tried to break down a dogged Hull side. They had not beaten Arsenal in 14 attempts since winning on their first visit to this ground in 2008. But with 20 minutes to play, there was still every chance that Sergej Jakirovic’s team could have pulled off one of the shocks of the season. Arsenal had already been denied a penalty just before half-time for a shirt pull on Kai Havertz in the box a week after escaping the same crime against Liverpool at Anfield, in a moment of controversy that could have been the major talking point from this match. Martin Ødegaard had other ideas and the Arsenal captain’s fifth goal of the season was enough to ensure they will go into the international break with a healthy lead over Manchester City. Enzo Maresca’s side are up next here in the league after the international break, with Arsenal having matched their record tally of 27 points from their opening 10 games. The signs look ominous for the rest, even if they were made to work for the points throughout by their opponents. Continue reading...

With the transfer window in full swing in July 2025, the former Manchester City scout and agent was not expecting to come face to face with a “footballing alien”, but that proved the case during a visit to Rapid Vienna’s training ground. A few weeks later, Sangaré moved to Lens for around €5m. “He was impressive and what struck me was his technique and his work rate,” Bengelloun says. That’s more or less the impression Sangaré has made at every club he’s played for, including Brentford, for whom the Mali midfielder signed, from Lens, for a club-record £39m at the start of August. The 24-year-old excelled in his debut against Tottenham a few weeks later , dominating the centre of the pitch and providing the assist for Keane Lewis-Potter’s opening goal, and has featured in every game this season, with Brighton up next. “I gave him his debut for Mali in September 2024, against Mozambique. He made an immediate impact,” says Sangaré’s former international manager Tom Saintfiet. “He’s every manager’s dream player.” Continue reading...

item.title: Chelsea’s Alonso identity still to form in a midfield that remains a problem
item.description: Roméo Lavia’s resurgence is not enough as injuries to other key players such as Moisés Caicedo are proving disruptive Xabi Alonso played for Pep Guardiola at Bayern Munich and was a key figure for Spain when their midfield dominated international football between 2008 and 2012. item.title: Rise of the ‘schooligans’: how a wave of antisocial behaviour threatens non-league football
item.description: Teenage ultras are increasingly causing disorder and communities fear it will not be long before it becomes something more dangerous It is five past three on Saturday afternoon and the teenage ultras of Hednesford Town are running late. They have arrived in Chester for their team’s National League North fixture and have hailed taxis, determined to make their presence felt at the ground. But word appears to have got out about their arrival. As one car turns away from the city’s charming half-timbered houses and into narrow residential streets, half a dozen local youths appear, haring round the corner in balaclavas. They try to attack the cab and chase after it as it pulls away. The smell of pyro is everywhere. As the taxi finally gets clear, the Chester gang stops in the middle of the road, shouting and gesticulating. One lad, no older than 16, pulls a long blade from inside his trousers and brandishes it. The incident ended there and no one was hurt, though a police investigation has been launched. The match went off without trouble too and the Hednesford gang – known at home as the “schooligans” – were escorted safely back to the station by Cheshire police. It was just another weekend in English non-league football, where a wave of antisocial behaviour is causing concern and leading the UK Football Policing Unit (UKFPU) to declare it its “most important” priority. As the disorder continues, a question remains: how long will it be before teenage trouble-making becomes something more dangerous? Continue reading...

item.title: Football Daily | You want proper football? Here are the FA Cup first-round ties to look out for
item.description: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now! For the FA Cup, the early rounds are the juice. The first round proper to be played out over the long weekend is looking, well, proper. And on Saturday at 3pm GMT, a proper time, 31 ties will kick off. No VAR, either. At the stage when the bottom two Football League divisions join the competition, focus remains on those non-league clubs fighting for the honour of the pyramid … John Aloisi winning or choking​ the Chinese Super League , a league so ‘super’ that nine of all 16 clubs in it started the season on negative points due to ‘match-fixing, gambling and corruption’ by the way, and the league leaders not even scoring a single goal in seven hours, is really not something to lay upon someone with a bad hangover. Apropos of nothing, if anyone has any objections to my views on the Chinese Super League, please address any correspondence to: Mr K Mbappé, Madrid (there’s no point two of us getting into trouble)” – Noble Francis. As a man of a certain age frequently being reminded of how out of date I am, the recent readers’ letters regarding technical solutions to shirt-pulling (Football Daily letters passim) concerns triggered distant memories. In late 1991 I was working in the Patents Advice Centre, Newcastle Central Library. A gentleman asked for help to possibly patent an ‘invention’: a football shirt with the seams held together by Velcro, so that any tug would ‘open’ the seam and provide clear evidence to the referee of illegal cloth gathering. As I helped him search for possible equivalent innovations in our paper database (yes kids!) we chatted amiably until I asked how he had come to this seemingly simple yet brilliant innovation. He paused, reddened and began to exhale with elevated pressure: ‘Did you see Arsenal the other night? Tony Adams? Disgraceful. It should never be allowed! In fact, with this shirt it won’t be, and Arsenal will have to learn to defend decently!’ Happy memories, obviously irrelavant to the modern game” – Garren Mulloy. Not fair! Bias! (Picture me, arms wide out, mouth open, eyebrows as high as they’ll go, appealing for reason.) I wrote about skin-tight shirts the other day and you ignored it, publishing a Velcro alternative. Now you’ve published another letter about skin-tight shirts ( yesterday’s letters ), days later. And it gets letter o’ the day! What’s the literary equivalent of kicking the keeper’s water bottle in frustration? I’ve just done that” – Ken Muir. I see that Celtic finally moved up the Bigger Vase charts on Thursday night and started playing a tune when their subs Osmand, Durán and Donovan came on. Too corny but my wife actually laughed at this” – Hugh Jamieson. That was a topsy-turvy Durán Durán show at Celtic, but what else would you expect from a bunch of Wild Bhoys?” – Peter Oh. Silence accompanied the funeral cortege as its made way from the funeral home to the parish church of San Miguel Arcángel carrying Jesús de Miguel Alameda, “Demi”, the Tenerife striker who died after an on-field collision with the Andorra goalkeeper Jesús Owono three days earlier. Only 3,587 people live in his family’s village but now they were joined by the game he loved. “We wanted to be close to his parents, his wife and daughter. In moments of pain, football comes together more than ever,” said Luis de la Fuente. The Spain manager did not say much else; there was not much else he could say, not much anyone could. These have been dark, desperate days, days when it was impossible to assimilate what has happened, and there will be more. “We will get through this together but we will need help, professional help,” the Tenerife president, Felipe Miñambres, said. item.title: Cristiano Ronaldo merely the latest example of a great player who couldn’t let go | Jonathan Wilson
item.description: There is no doubt his international career was an incredible one, but it would have been greater still if he had not lingered on the stage so long Nothing, perhaps, is quite so difficult for an elite sportsperson as timing their exit. It’s not easy for any person in any job to weigh the hope of having more to give with the desire not to linger beyond their usefulness, but it’s perhaps particularly hard for top athletes because unrealistic self-confidence is so essential to their success. It takes an almost unhealthy level of self-belief for anybody to make the sacrifices to get to the top, to dedicate themselves to such a precarious vocation, to overcome all the setbacks and injuries and failures. How can someone – whose whole life has been spent assuring themselves there are no odds they cannot overcome – accept that is it, that the time has come to say goodbye? The news that Cristiano Ronaldo has retired from international football brings with it, inevitably, a sadness. Sadness we will no longer see him skipping past a defender, or burying a neck-thrusting header, and sadness in that the end of the career of any great is a reminder of mortality; all things in time must pass. But there is also a sadness he timed his departure so badly. For at least three tournaments, there has been a sense of Ronaldo holding Portugal back. Continue reading...

Sevastopol were declared champions of group one in Football National League (FNL) 2B, in effect Russia’s fourth division, last month and are believed to have applied for a licence to compete at the level above. Should it be granted and they proceed to FNL 2A, it would appear a violation of Uefa rules that prohibit Crimean clubs from playing in competitions organised by the Russian Football Union (RFU). The governing body would come under severe pressure to extend sanctions on European football’s pariah state, whose club and national teams are banned from competing in international tournaments. item.title: Has a footballer ever run a marathon faster than James Milner? | The Knowledge
item.description: Plus: managers sacked after signing new deals, war victims commemorated on kits and the first club website (part II) Mail us with all of your questions and answers It came as no surprise to the Knowledge that James Milner had spent the early months of his retirement training for – and then running in – the New York City Marathon. Yes, the bleep test-loving former Brighton, Liverpool and Manchester City player recorded an excellent time of 3hr 9min 4sec, an average of 7min 13sec per mile. Not bad for a 40-year-old whose physique is more like that of a wrestler than a whippet. “A few years ago, I feel like I could have definitely done sub-3:00,” he said, lamenting his late-career injuries for hindering him. In 2012 we ran a column listing footballers’ fastest marathon times, with the former Leicester playmaker Muzzy Izzet leading the pack on 3hr 22min 36sec at the 2011 London Marathon. item.title: Harry Kane’s Ballon d’Or party gives way to anxiety-filled hangover for Bayern Munich | Andy Brassell
item.description: Dortmund did not read the script, remaining level on points with the defending champions at the top of the table It was the moment they had all been … not so much waiting for, but planning, pushing and yearning for. In the videos that announce the starting lineup on the giant scoreboard before kick-off, every Bayern Munich player turns to face the camera with their personal salute, greeting or goal celebration, the playful progression from the standard folding of arms. Except on Saturday evening, the No 9 turned around smiling, and cradling the golden trophy. In the midweek DFB Pokal stroll against Magdeburg there had been a salute, the players welcoming Harry Kane on to the pitch with a guard of honour to commemorate his Ballon d’Or victory two nights before. This, however, was the real party, the moment where the England captain’s and Bayern’s successful union and the apex it has reached was celebrated in front of a global audience. There was every reason to believe it would be a full and satisfying victory lap, even in Der Klassiker, with proper competition so often bringing the best out of the Rekordmeister. item.title: Folarin Balogun takes a first, tiny step toward moving on from a calamitous summer
item.description: The USMNT striker scored his first goal since the World Cup in a losing effort against Paris FC. Could it lead to something more? Before this weekend, the last time Folarin Balogun scored was in the United States’ 2-0 win over Bosnia and Herzegovina at this past summer’s World Cup. In the immediate aftermath, the outlook for Balogun seemed rosy; an ascendant player who could muster a goal in tense games. At half-time against Bosnia, US fans weren’t just wondering how far his team could advance – they were sizing Balogun up against some of the world’s best strikers. But for most of the ensuing four months, Balogun has been in limbo. His breakout World Cup was overshadowed by a red card in that same game against Bosnia and Herzegovina, followed by a scandal of which he wanted no part. Just as it seemed a summer move away from Monaco could get his club career on track, he broke off a possible deadline-day move to Everton after a lengthy visit to the training grounds and a medical he felt was improperly handled. item.title: Rampant Salford hint that Beckham’s lofty ambitions are not a pipe dream
item.description: The aim of reaching the Championship looks more realistic for a Manchester club in the shadow of City and United After seven seasons in League Two, Salford City are finally threatening to match the hype brought by their high-profile owners. First it was the Class of ’92 who guided them up through the non-league system into the fourth tier but failed to progress any further. Gary Neville and David Beckham remain, part of a new group that took over in May 2025, with this year beginning to look transformational after securing an eighth straight win, against Exeter, to put them five points clear at the top. The budget has increased, allowing the club to sign a number of players who will feel they are above League Two standard. Striker Macaulay Langstaff arrived from Millwall; the last time he played at this level, he scored 28 league goals in a season for Notts County. Match-winner Will Aimson spent the past two seasons in the division above with Wigan and has dropped down because of Salford’s project. Continue reading...

item.title: Mourinho’s plan comes together as Real Madrid relaunch with clásico statement | Sid Lowe
item.description: It was just like old times as José Mourinho ended a night at Camp Nou with a knee slide and three points José Mourinho had already done the por qu é? , the printout and the press conference no-show in under 100 days. Now he’s done a knee slide too, and in the perfect place: back where it all began and where it can all begin again. When Kylian Mbappé scored the first in the clásico on Sunday night, Real Madrid’s manager hardly moved, sitting in the shadow of the bench – but when the striker got the second to win it with time running out, that was different. Mourinho leapt into the light, throwing himself to the grass, the knees of a 63-year-old’s trousers muddy as a schoolboy’s, stuck his tongue out and pumped his fists. He does so love it when a plan comes together. To the right of him, the bench was emptying, subs joining the players in sprinting towards the south-west corner. As they leapt about, dodging the bottles thrown towards them from the end, way, way up in the furthest corner and stuck inside a glass box like a bunch of David Blaines, the small group of Madrid fans who had come were going mad. In the main stand, a thousand phones were raised. And 600 kilometres west, back in Boadilla, Thibaut Courtois was watching his teammates from the sofa at home, presumably wrapped in a blanket and cradling a cup of Lemsip. On the morning of the biggest game there is, he awoke with flu, forced to miss out. Continue reading...

item.title: The horse that ushered in Manchester United’s tragic arc | Jonathan Wilson
item.description: There’s plenty of blame to go around at Old Trafford. Like all downfalls it started with a seemingly small, unconnected moment Sign up for our free newsletter here And so here we are again, at that point as the nights draw in and Manchester United prepare to sack a manager . Autumn: season of mists, mellow fruitfulness and a crisis at Old Trafford. Sunday’s 3-0 home defeat to Bournemouth , coming on the back of last week’s 4-1 reverse against Como, made clear what many had feared from the moment Michael Carrick was given the job on a permanent basis: that he isn’t up to it. But then, who could be? When you’ve burned through a long list of managers in 13 years, it’s perhaps worth considering whether the manager is really the problem. Could some blame perhaps go to the director of football, Jason Wilcox, or the chief executive, Omar Berrada, the people making the appointments? Or perhaps to Sir Jim Ratcliffe, the cost-cutting tax exile and minority shareholder with responsibility for sporting operations? Or to the Glazer family, who plunged the club into debt with a leveraged buyout in 2005 and have since made calamitous decision after calamitous decision, reducing the most successful club in English league history to a mid-table laughing stock with a roof that leaks symbolically ? This is an extract from Soccer Desk, a newsletter from the Guardian US. Subscribe for free here . Continue reading...

item.title: Next Generation 2021: why slow and steady sometimes wins the race
item.description: Our NextGen picks from five years ago show that breaking through early does not guarantee longevity or future success Read the full updates on our class of 2021 here and here In 2021, as every year, we picked 80 players from around the world who had a chance of making it in world football – 20 from the Premier League and 60 from the rest of the world – as part of our Next Generation series . We then follow these talented boys on their journeys for five years. Often it is almost impossible to predict how they will get on (OK, when Sid Lowe sent over Lamine Yamal in 2024 we had an inkling he might do well). The ball-playing central midfielder comes from a footballing family and academy staff believe his tactical awareness is born from growing up around the game. His father, Adam, played for Brighton and is now manager along the coast at Worthing FC, while Martin (his great uncle), Paul (his grandad), and Wally (his great grandad), all enjoyed careers as players. The youngest to play in the Bundesliga at 16 years and one day, youngest player to appear in the Champions League 17 days later, youngest goal scorer in Bundesliga 11 days after that and youngest player and youngest goal scorer for the Germany Under-21 team before he has turned 17. item.title: Aitana Bonmatí makes Guardian top 100 history with third title in a row
item.description: The margin may have got smaller but the brilliant Spanish midfielder makes it a hat-trick of No 1 finishes They say the best things come in threes, and Aitana Bonmatí has written herself into the Guardian’s top 100 history as the first player to finish at the top of the tree for a third consecutive year. Last year the majestic midfielder emulated her Barcelona and Spain teammate Alexia Putellas by winning for a second year running , but the 27-year-old has now gone one better, establishing herself once again at the top of the women’s game.
